input.quote: 14.5 Independent Contractors. The parties are independent contractors with respect to each other. Each party is not and shall not be deemed to be an employee, agent, partner or legal representative of the other for any purpose and shall not have any right, power or authority to create any obligation or responsibility on behalf of the other.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-inducement covenant at all. Searches for "solicit", "hire", "recruit", "induce" and "employ" return no hiring restriction, a sweep of every "shall not" obligation surfaces only IP, confidentiality, trademark and covenant-not-to-sue restrictions, and full reads of the likely homes for such a covenant (§ 10 Confidentiality, § 13 Shared Resources, § 14 Miscellaneous and Exhibit D § 5 Personnel) confirm none exists. The only personnel-related provisions are § 13.5's Commerce One employee NDA/invention warranty, § 14.5's independent contractor language and Exhibit D § 5's staffing commitment, none of which restricts Corio (our party) from soliciting, hiring or engaging Commerce One personnel. This is the rule's preferred position — no non-solicit binds the Customer — so the finding is compliant and no redline is proposed. The failed deterministic checks for a duration limit and a general-solicitation carve-out are artefacts of there being no restrictive covenant to qualify, not evidence of a deficient clause; if Commerce One later proposes a non-solicit, our fallback is a mutual 12-month restriction limited to personnel directly involved in the services with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire.
